claims.text: An ML-accelerated free-energy integration scheme can accurately capture solid-state free energies near fusion.
The scheme can accurately capture fluid-state free energies near fusion.
The scheme can retain vibrational, anharmonic, and electron-vibration contributions to free energy.
Interatomic-potential surrogates are viable for multicomponent high-entropy alloys with at least five principal elements.
Full ab initio molecular dynamics would be replaced by an ML-learned free-energy integration workflow using sparse, targeted ab initio calculations.
The workflow would monitor predicted forces or energies and trigger ab initio recalibration when deviations exceed set thresholds.
The ML potential would sample configurational space rapidly.
Periodic recalibration would ensure accurate incorporation of vibrational, anharmonic, and electron-vibration entropy contributions.
Dynamic recalibration would maintain ab initio fidelity in the calculated phase free energies.
The method would reproduce fusion free energies, melting temperatures, and latent heats with accuracy comparable to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
The method would achieve a 10- to 100-fold computational speedup relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
The method would provide higher throughput than TOR-TILD for multicomponent systems.
TOR-TILD calculations are primarily established for elemental and binary systems.
Anharmonic and electron-vibration effects are significant in the specified near-fusion temperature regime.
The proposed method is intended to apply from elemental and binary systems through high-entropy alloys containing five or more principal elements.
Errors greater than 5% relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics results in key derived observables would falsify the hypothesis.
